title: Widespread order-submission failures in the Order Management Service
alert_or_symptom: A large proportion of customer order submissions are failing, while customers can still browse products, authenticate and view existing orders.

technical_evidence.observation: Order creation success fell from 99.5 percent to 27.8 percent at 10:12 across the United Kingdom and Ireland storefronts.
Failed order submissions generate an unhandled PromotionValidationException in the Order Management Service before the order persistence stage.
Failed requests stop inside the Order Management Service promotion-validation handler before calls are made to the Transaction Database Cluster, Inventory Service or Message Broker.
The Transaction Database Cluster, Inventory Service, Message Broker, Application Compute Cluster and Public API Gateway are healthy and operating normally.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Approximately 72 percent of customer order submissions fail before an order is created, although browsing, authentication and existing-order retrieval remain available.
service_impact.business_function_affected: Customer order creation and checkout completion

environmental_context: The Order Management Service calls the Transaction Database Cluster, Inventory Service and Message Broker after application-level order validation.
The supplied traces show that failed requests do not reach those dependencies.

recent_changes.description: An Order Management Service promotion-rule library update was deployed at 09:35.

reported_unknowns: It has not been confirmed whether the business-to-business order API is affected by the same application failure.
The expected duration of the order-submission degradation is not yet known.
additional_context: No duplicate orders, unintended order records, data loss or security exposure have been observed.
